content:
ashley: ran a focused profile on host tokenization + parse for DRP traffic, seeing ~12-18% CPU on preparse for short requests, spikes up to 30% on grpc streaming bursts. attaching quick notes.

sam: timeline? can you paste the flame or top lines? :eyes:

ashley: quick top lines from perf report:
```
host_parse 12.3%
grpc_read 8.1%
tokenizer::split 7.9%
kv_prefetch 5.4%
stream_chunker::assemble 4.7%
```
most of host_parse is memcpy + header parse; tokenization is small but hot for many tiny requests.

marco: is this messing up batching heuristics? i remember small preparse tails causing the minibatcher window to close early.

ashley: exactly. preparse latency pushes requests past minibatch window so kernel selector sees lower batch sizes -> throughput hit. saw median batch_size drop from 8 -> 3 on affected p95 traffic.

nina: any quick wins we can try before a larger refactor? async tokenize or move minimal parse into the ingress sidecar?

ashley: prototyped async sidecar tokenize. baseline: sidecar adds a hop but moves CPU off host. For 1-5 token requests saw ~20% end-to-end improvement for host CPU and p50 latency. prototype outline:
```
// sidecar pretokenize API
POST /_pretokenize
body: {"text": "..."}
return: {"tokens": [...], "count": N}
```
tradeoffs: RPC overhead + TLS, need backpressure.

pranav: can we also add a JSON fast-path for header parsing? most requests only need route,user,streaming_flag.

ashley: implemented a tiny fastjson that extracts those 3 fields inline -> shaved ~6% CPU on host_parse. will include patch.

sam: what about the streaming chunker? we had earlier grpc small-write thrash causing syscall storms.

ashley: found fragmentation from writev flush frequency. coalescing window tweak (2ms -> 5ms) reduced syscall rate and smoothed tail latency. simple change in coalescer:
```
coalesce_ms = 5
if pending_bytes < threshold -> delay flush until window expires
```
improved p95 for stream bursts by ~10%.

perf-bot: canary perf summary: host CPU per-request down 14% for short requests, p95 latency down 8%. all canary checks PASS.

nina: plan: RFC + canary rollout. add telemetry for batch_size, preparse_latency, kernel_selected, and stream_flush_rate.

marco: +1. include correlation slices by request token count and model family so we can confirm kernel selection shifts back to larger batches.

ashley: will open PR + RFC this afternoon and draft canary plan (target small worker pool first). cc @sam @marco @nina.

sam: thanks — happy to help with telemetry dashboards.

ashley: awesome, will drop initial numbers in the RFC and link the profiling flame gist. :thumbsup:
